answers.question: Are there known failure cases or past conversations the agent must handle, beyond a customer with two open orders who says "cancel my order"?
answers.reply:
> No transcripts or known incidents. Known failure cases to cover:
> 2. Cancel succeeded, refund call returned an error — refund not issued, state known; agent reports it, does not claim success, hands off to the store's manual refund process. One retry allowed on a transient error, none on a terminal one.
> 3. Cancel succeeded, refund call timed out — state unknown; agent retries once, then re-reads the order and refund records and reports what it finds. Final message must match the final refund status.
> Derive any further cases yourself.

answers.question: When the refund the order system reports has an amount or a payment method different from the one the customer said yes to, what does the agent do?
answers.recommended: The agent makes no further change with the new value, tells the customer the amount and payment method the order system returned, and hands the case to staff with a follow-up task.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> Proposed default: the agent cancels an order only after the customer explicitly confirms the full proposal (which order, the refund amount and where it goes); any change after confirmation voids it.

answers.question: How many orders may the agent cancel in one conversation, and what ends it?
answers.recommended: One order per proposal. After one order is done, the customer may name another of their orders, and the agent starts over with a new proposal and a new yes. It ends when the customer names no other order to cancel.
